 Here's Why Sterlite Technologies (NSE:STLTECH) Has Caught The Eye Of Investors
 October 26, 2026 SI Simply Wall St The excitement of investing in a company that can reverse its fortunes is a big draw for some speculators, so even companies that have no revenue, no profit, and a record of falling short, can manage to find investors. Sometimes these stories can cloud the minds of investors, leading them to invest with their emotions rather than on the merit of good company fundamentals. A loss-making company is yet to prove itself with profit, and eventually the inflow of external capital may dry up. 
 In contrast to all that, many investors prefer to focus on companies like Sterlite Technologies ( NSE:STLTECH ), which has not only revenues, but also profits. While profit isn't the sole metric that should be considered when investing, it's worth recognising businesses that can consistently produce it.

 Advertisement Sterlite Technologies' Earnings Per Share Are Growing 
 The market is a voting machine in the short term, but a weighing machine in the long term, so you'd expect share price to follow earnings per share (EPS) outcomes eventually. Therefore, there are plenty of investors who like to buy shares in companies that are growing EPS. It certainly is nice to see that Sterlite Technologies has managed to grow EPS by 35% per year over three years. As a result, we can understand why the stock trades on a high multiple of trailing twelve month earnings. 
 Careful consideration of revenue growth and earnings before interest and taxation (EBIT) margins can help inform a view on the sustainability of the recent profit growth. The good news is that Sterlite Technologies is growing revenues, and EBIT margins improved by 11.3 percentage points to 16%, over the last year. Ticking those two boxes is a good sign of growth, in our book.

 Fortunately, we've got access to analyst forecasts of Sterlite Technologies' future profits. You can do your own forecasts without looking, or you can take a peek at what the professionals are predicting . 
 Are Sterlite Technologies Insiders Aligned With All Shareholders?
 It should give investors a sense of security owning shares in a company if insiders also own shares, creating a close alignment their interests. So it is good to see that Sterlite Technologies insiders have a significant amount of capital invested in the stock. To be specific, they have ₹2.3b worth of shares. That shows significant buy-in, and may indicate conviction in the business strategy. Despite being just 0.5% of the company, the value of that investment is enough to show insiders have plenty riding on the venture. 
 It means a lot to see insiders invested in the business, but shareholders may be wondering if remuneration policies are in their best interest. Our quick analysis into CEO remuneration would seem to indicate they are. Our analysis has discovered that the median total compensation for the CEOs of companies like Sterlite Technologies with market caps between ₹190b and ₹608b is about ₹64m. 
 Sterlite Technologies' CEO took home a total compensation package worth ₹38m in the year leading up to March 2026. That is actually below the median for CEO's of similarly sized companies. CEO remuneration levels are not the most important metric for investors, but when the pay is modest, that does support enhanced alignment between the CEO and the ordinary shareholders. It can also be a sign of good governance, more generally. 
 Is Sterlite Technologies Worth Keeping An Eye On? 
 You can't deny that Sterlite Technologies has grown its earnings per share at a very impressive rate. That's attractive. If you need more convincing beyond that EPS growth rate, don't forget about the reasonable remuneration and the high insider ownership. Everyone has their own preferences when it comes to investing but it definitely makes Sterlite Technologies look rather interesting indeed. Of course, profit growth is one thing but it's even better if Sterlite Technologies is receiving high returns on equity, since that should imply it can keep growing without much need for capital. The key swing factor is whether agentic AI traffic inspection and data security add-ons lift net new ARR, or whether the zero trust platform consolidation just offsets pricing pressure from Palo Alto and Cloudflare. I'd watch FCF margin (guided 23-23.5%) and SBC dilution as the main risks if growth stays near 17%.

I'd watch net revenue retention and how much of the FY31 $8-10B ARR target depends on new AI-security products versus plain seat growth. At a ~7% discount to fair value the margin of safety is thin if growth slips below the high teens.
